criteria.rationale: Verified: Go's Wait returns ErrWaitDelay only when the process itself succeeded and the pipes outlived WaitDelay, and an ExitError takes precedence (probed: exit 3 with a lingering child is recorded failed, exit status 3). Verified: an unstaged move shows as D plus ??, a staged one as R old -> new, both now checked. Accepted risk, already in the spec: the reviewer runs with the user's permissions and can write outside the worktree or hide edits from git status (skip-worktree, a corrupted worktree index; the status error is ignored); the check targets accidental edits by a configured adapter, not a hostile one.

The adapter runs in its own process group (Setpgid); ctx cancellation kills the group, the group is killed again after Run, and WaitDelay 5s bounds pipe draining. TestReviewDispatchTimeoutKillsTheAdaptersChildren returns in under a second; TestReviewDispatchJudgesTheRunNotItsLeftovers fails on 484a9459 (checked by reverting internal/pose/review_dispatch.go) and passes on HEAD. Deferred worktree removal runs before the temp dir removal (LIFO). On Windows no group kill exists, so a lingering child of a successful run survives the run; documented in review_dispatch_windows.go, low.

Additive: a new subcommand, a new optional policy file .pose/policy/reviewers.json (schema_version 1, absent means no adapter) and new records under .pose/review-runs/. No existing attestation, bundle or CLI contract changes; mcp-review-attest-integration and the review suites pass unchanged. The dispatch path itself is exercised end to end through the CLI in pose-mcp/go/test (unit class in the matrix).

Policy is validated on load (schema_version, command/vendor/model required, timeout parsed); an unknown adapter lists the configured ones; a sealed commit absent from the repository is refused before any worktree; missing --via or target is a usage error.
Dispatch only reads bundles and briefs and writes .pose/review-runs; it records no attestation (R5), so verify and close are unaffected; the review attestation integration check passes unchanged.

Each run records adapter, vendor, model, times, exit code, brief and transcript digests, the transcript and a failure reason naming the changed paths, the timeout or the command error. No secrets are written beyond what the adapter prints.
Nothing existing changes shape; an instance without reviewers.json behaves as before and dispatch then prints the example policy and the brief (R6).

Reviewed all four commits with the trailer (d7240e36, 59aab417, 484a9459, 73cda152), both fixes against the findings of the second review. Probed with temporary adapters (removed): staged rename into '.pose/state/a b é.go' fails naming pose-mcp/lib.go; staged edit fails; an untracked 'new file.go' fails; a commit fails as moved off the sealed commit; exit 3 with a lingering child fails. Builds for linux, windows and darwin. pose validate --tolerant --json-out .pose/results/delivery-validation.json at 73cda152 with the candidate CLI built from it: 131 of 131 steps pass, including pose-mcp/go/test, which runs TestReviewDispatchRunsAndRecordsAdapters, TestReviewDispatchRecordsEveryBriefKind, TestReviewDispatchTimeoutKillsTheAdaptersChildren and TestReviewDispatchJudgesTheRunNotItsLeftovers.

The derived-state allowlist answers the first real run's false failure; process groups answer the hang; accepting ErrWaitDelay only on a successful ProcessState answers the false failure on exit 0; splitting the rename answers the destination-only check. assess design observed the subject.

Help catalog names review dispatch; the spec, execution log and changelog fragment describe the adapter policy, the run record and the residual risks. Applied the review workflow, security and documentation-style rules.
With no adapter the command prints the example policy and the brief instead of failing silently; failures name what changed or why; exit code 1 on a failed run.

R1-R7 each map to a passing test in the trace; checked the example adapters enable nothing (ExampleReviewersPolicy is only printed), the worktree is detached at the sealed head and removed, brief on stdin, budget counted per adapter per bundle.

Matches the Technical Plan artifacts; no attestation recording, which stays with pose-delegated-review-capability. Reviewer prefix agent:independent-claude-opus-5-5-review is a declaration the engine requires. This review is another execution of the same vendor and model as the implementer (Claude Opus 5.5, agent:claude-opus-5-5), run as fallback because the other-vendor reviewer (Codex) was unavailable: independence of execution, not of vendor. The maintainer authorised this use.

The user's working tree is not written by the reviewer process (disposable detached worktree); argv is a list, no shell interpolation by POSE; {output} is a temp path. Residual risk recorded in the spec: the adapter runs with user permissions; the examples run read-only.
One store function, one CLI command, two tiny platform files; no daemon or sandbox layer, which the ADR leaves to the adapter.
